speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing neck and arm pain, along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To understand the cause of these symptoms, could you tell me if the pain radiates from your neck specifically down into your shoulder or arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The burning pain and paresthesias suggest nerve involvement; has this pain radiates specifically down your arms or into your fingers? Additionally, could you describe whether your weakness affects your grip strength or makes daily tasks like buttoning shirts difficult?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with concurrent cervical radiculopathy.

The combination of upper motor neuron signs (burning pain radiating, though less common in pure ALS) and distinct lower motor neuron signs (fasciculations, absent reflexes, and muscle weakness) in a 58-year-old male is highly suggestive of ALS. Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, I must rule out cervical myelopathy or severe radiculopathy as a mimic. I am ordering an MRI of your Cervical Spine and Nerve Conduction Studies (EMG/NCS) to differentiate between a compressive lesion and a primary motor neuron disease.
